changes.quote: 2019 | Up To 60 Months 4, 6 · 6 To qualify for terms greater than 48 months, borrowers must have a minimum Credit Bureau Risk Score (FICO) > 750
changes.note: The max-term-by-model-year table was missing. Six rows, transcribed with their footnote conditions. The one that matters and was nowhere in the record: on a 2019 or older unit, any term over 48 months requires FICO 750+. The record only carried the 750 rule for 2021-2020 over 66 months, so a 675-score customer on a 2019 car looked eligible for 60 months when the sheet caps them at 48. Also adds US Bank's own front-end vs total LTV definitions.

ambiguities.note: Most of this record is right. The 4-row front-end advance / total LTV table (2027-2019 at 740+/700-739/675-699 and 2018-2017 at 675+), the KBB state list, the CPO enhancement (+$500 under $40K, +$1,000 at or above, applied systemically), the 100,001-125,000 mile term caps, the 30/45-day payment window, the $5,000 minimum ($10,000 in NJ) and the back-end ceiling of $5,500 or 20% all match the sheet.

Record describes flats of 1-4.5%, markup caps and a $10,000 maximum. This sheet says only "Refer to the U.S. Bank National Installment Auto Finance Program Rules" for both loan processing fees and dealer participation. The numbers must come from the separate Program Rules PDF (1GVzTsNCRy1Dm7gdHEIfzZ3DoYS31EumL), which I did not read here. Unverified.
